selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act of 2025 makes changes to prior authorization rules under Medicare Advantage plans. The bill requires Medicare Advantage plans to set up electronic prior authorization programs, meet certain transparency rules by submitting annual data to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, and follow enrollee protection standards. It also directs federal agencies to report on data analysis, real-time decision-making feasibility, and the impact of artificial intelligence on patient access.

affected_groups.effect: Receive protection standards, electronic prior authorization processes, and increased transparency regarding plan criteria and prior authorization denials or approvals.

Gain access to secure electronic transmission methods for prior authorization requests, transparent plan lists, criteria, and potential waivers or modifications of requirements based on compliance performance.

Must implement electronic prior authorization systems, submit detailed annual transparency data to the government, comply with new response timeframes, and participate in federal reporting evaluations.
Required to collect plan data, publish reports on automated decision-making and artificial intelligence impacts, and submit evaluation reports to Congress.

key_provisions: Medicare Advantage plans must establish an electronic prior authorization program starting on or after January 1, 2028, which excludes facsimiles and non-compliant portals.

Plans must meet transparency requirements starting on or after January 1, 2027, by annually submitting prior authorization data—such as approval rates, denial rates, appeal outcomes, and processing times—to the Secretary.

Plans must adopt enrollee protection standards, including developing transparent programs with input from enrollees and providers, allowing waivers based on provider compliance, and conducting annual reviews.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology must publish a report detailing real-time decisions, routinely approved items and services, and the impact of artificial intelligence.

The Secretary of Health and Human Services is given the authority to establish specific timeframes for responses to prior authorization requests, such as 24-hour windows for expedited or real-time decisions.
missing_information: Specific technical standards for compliant electronic prior authorization programs beyond exclusions.
Exact numerical thresholds for provider waiver performance standards.
Specific funding amounts or budgetary impacts associated with implementing the required electronic systems and federal reports.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act of 2025 makes changes to prior authorization rules under Medicare Advantage plans. The bill requires Medicare Advantage plans to set up electronic prior authorization programs, meet certain transparency rules by submitting annual data to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, and follow enrollee protection standards. It also directs federal agencies to report on data analysis, real-time decision-making feasibility, and the impact of artificial intelligence on patient access.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation places systematic federal requirements on Medicare Advantage prior authorization procedures, mandating electronic processing, comprehensive data transparency, and adherence to specific response times and standards. The score for significance is 75 because it broadly alters administrative requirements for all Medicare Advantage plans and touches the vast majority of participating healthcare providers and senior enrollees.
